ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, counterparties, smelters, brokers, and consignees against the UN Consolidated List, Canadian SEMA and UN Act listings, OFAC SDN list for USD-clearing exposure, and EU consolidated lists. PEP screening under PCMLTFA Part 12.1 (domestic PEPs) and Part 12.2 (foreign PEPs) is conducted by the onboarding bank; the ULC must complete enhanced due diligence questionnaires and document source of funds and source of wealth for every controlling person. Scrap-purchase records must capture seller identification, payment method, and compliance with Alberta cash-purchase prohibitions to mitigate metal-theft proceeds integration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry - myCORES (official government portal alberta.ca/corporate-registry, operated through licensed registry agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registered names must use English or French letters with standard punctuation; non-Roman scripts such as Chinese characters, Cyrillic, or Arabic are not registrable in provincial corporate names. A parallel trade name in a foreign script is permitted only as an informal translation and does not appear on the Certificate of Incorporation. Required ULC designators: 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', 'Societe a responsabilite illimitee', or 'SRI'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Crown; Royal; Federal; Government; Municipal; Police
Canadian; Canada; Alberta (where implying government sponsorship or misleading territorial scope)
Terms suggesting a regulated profession or securities/money-services activity without the applicable licence
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS name search report must accompany the name reservation application; the reservation is valid for 90 days and may be extended once for a further 90 days if the name remains available. Upon rejection, the applicant may (i) file a new NUANS search with a modulated name; (ii) submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar of Corporations (Service Alberta) within 30 days, citing distinctive elements distinguishing the proposed name; or (iii) apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review under the Business Corporations Act. All appeals should be lodged before the reservation window lapses to avoid re-running the NUANS process.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Registered office: permissible where a physical street address in Alberta is provided by a registered agent or serviced-office provider and corporate records, including the ISC register, are maintained there. Commercial substance: a letterbox-only presence entails high denial risk for bank onboarding, documentary LC issuance, provincial scrap-metal licensing, and GST account approval; a lease or storage contract for a yard or warehouse, evidence of local management, and operational records are strongly advisable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated: approximately 55-65% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 36 months, driven by Alberta Scrap Metals Dealers and Recyclers Act municipal licence inspections, environmental and civil enforcement checks, FINTRAC examinations of the banking channel, and CRA field audits of GST and cross-border payments.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended — incorporation of an Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) under Part 1 (ss. 9-15), share subscription and consideration rules (Part 2), registered office and records (Part 3), directors and officers (Part 4/5), and the ULC unlimited liability designation set out in the articles of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Alberta Corporate Access 'AC Access' electronic portal; authorized corporate service providers).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1), together with the Certificate of Incorporation, Notice of Registered Office (Form 2), and Notice of Directors (Form 3) issued under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Alberta ULC and no escrow account requirement under the ABCA. Shares may be issued for any consideration acceptable to the directors in any currency; shares subscribed prior to incorporation must be accepted by the board and the consideration must be fully received before share certificates are issued. Non-resident ownership is permitted, but an Investment Canada Act notification applies to acquisitions of control by non-Canadians.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: (1) That the share subscriptions set forth in the subscription list are accepted and the corresponding shares are hereby issued for the consideration stated therein, which consideration has been duly received; (2) That the registered office of the Corporation is established at [Alberta Registered Office Address] and the Notice of Registered Office is to be filed with the Registrar of Corporations; (3) That the following officers are appointed to hold office until successors are elected: President, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary; (4) That the appointed officers are authorized, jointly and severally, to execute all documents, open bank accounts, and complete all filings required to give effect to the incorporation and to comply with applicable federal and provincial registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service Alberta Corporate Registry — Alberta Corporate Access (AC Access) or an authorized Service Alberta registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search (NUANS) request for the proposed corporate name ending in 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. Review the preliminary search for conflicting corporate names and trademarks; if clear, reserve the name for 90 days. E-signatures are accepted; notarization is not required for the reservation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (or numbered company election)
Alberta registered address for the name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a NUANS conflict or confusing similarity is identified, select an alternative name or obtain a written consent/agreement from the conflicting name holder and refile the search; a contested rejection may be appealed to the Service Alberta registry coordinator.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Incorporating Documents and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (pre-filing review) together with corporate legal counsel or an authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 – Articles of Incorporation, including unlimited liability share terms; draft Form 2 – Notice of Registered Office; complete Form 3 – Notice of Directors; execute the subscriber share subscription list and first director consents. Under the ABCA, notarization is not mandatory, but original or counterpart signatures must be retained.
required_dossiers: NUANS confirmation number and reservation certificate
Share subscription list and payment acknowledgement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registry pre-filing queries are cured by amending the affected forms and re-executing signatures; corrected pages may be resubmitted within the registry's deficiency notice period without additional fee unless the corporate name is changed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Certificate of Incorporation Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (AC Access online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the executed forms electronically through AC Access; pay the statutory incorporation fee (CAD 100) and the NUANS fee; upon approval, the registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation and returns the stamped Articles of Incorporation. Paper filings may be mailed to the Corporate Registry in Edmonton, with a longer processing period.
required_dossiers: Statutory fee payment (CAD 100 incorporation plus CAD 20 NUANS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected for a defect, the registry issues a deficiency notice; correct and resubmit the revised forms within the specified period; new fees apply only if a different corporate name must be searched.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Organization: Minute Book, Share Issuance, and Federal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online (BRO); corporate secretary and legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organization meeting and adopt the First Board Resolution; issue share certificates to subscribers; prepare the corporate minute book containing by-laws, registers of directors and shareholders, and the Certificate of Incorporation. Apply online with the CRA for the Business Number (BN), GST/HST account, and any import/export program accounts (customers/exporters 'RM' account) needed for the cross-border consignment of recycled scrap.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution and organizational minutes
RC165 – Request for a Business Number and CRA account setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA Business Number issuance is delayed, contact CRA Business Enquiries at 1-800-959-5525; if counterparties require authenticated corporate records, order certified copies from the Alberta Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal business licensing department in the municipality of the registered office (e.g., Calgary Licensing Program or Edmonton Business Licence Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a general business licence application with proof of incorporation, premises lease, site plan, and a municipal fire inspection certificate. If the municipality enforces a second-hand goods or scrap metal dealer by-law, apply for the supplemental dealer licence endorsement. Display the licence at the registered business premises before operations begin.
required_dossiers: Registered office or warehouse lease or ownership proof
Site and floor plan of storage yards and processing areas
Criminal record check of principals if required by municipal by-law
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal licence refusals may be appealed to the municipal licensing authority or designated appeal committee; remedy inspection deficiencies and resubmit. If zoning is incompatible, apply for a discretionary development permit or relocate to an appropriately zoned light-industrial site.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Scrap Metal Dealer Licence and Environmental Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicable municipal licensing authority administering the Scrap Metals Dealers Act (Alberta); environmental oversight by Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Scrap Metal Dealer Licence under the Scrap Metals Dealers Act (SA 2004, c S-14.5) and the enforcing municipal by-law; maintain records of cash transactions and seller identification. Determine whether the storage/processing activity is designated under the Activities Designation Regulation (A.R. 276/2003) and file an EPEA Registration if required. Secure the Alberta fire and occupational health clearances prior to commencing operations.
required_dossiers: EPEA registration application or self-classification report
Fire safety and occupational health clearance forms
Seller record-keeping policy and AML risk controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEPA determines that a full EPEA Approval is required, complete the environmental impact screening and apply under EPEA s. 66. If the dealer licence is refused, appeal to the municipality or the responsible provincial minister; remedy compliance deficiencies and request re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal licensing authorities administering the Scrap Metals Dealers Act (Alberta) (SA 2004, c S-14.5), with provincial policy oversight by Alberta Public Safety and environmental authority vested in Alberta Environment and Protected Areas.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Scrap Metal Dealer Licence under the Scrap Metals Dealers Act (Alberta) and the applicable municipal dealer by-law; supplemental EPEA Registration under the Activities Designation Regulation (A.R. 276/2003) where storage or processing thresholds are met.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EIA Exempt for wholesaling, consignment, sorting, baling, and storage of non-ferrous scrap; EPEA Registration is the applicable tier under the Activities Designation Regulation (A.R. 276/2003) for designated metal-scrap storage/processing facilities. A full EIA and EPEA Approval are reserved for smelting, refining, hazardous waste management, or operations that may discharge into a water body.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater discharge and containment of stormwater from outdoor storage yards using berms, covers, and oil/grit separators prior to release under an Alberta Water Act approval. Releases of any deleterious substances are reportable under the Release Reporting Regulation (A.R. 117/2018). Fugitive dust and particulate emissions must not cause exceedances of the Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives. VOC and odour controls (negative-pressure filtration or baghouse) are required if PVC-insulated copper wire is granulated or shredded. Non-hazardous residues and trace PCB-contaminated materials must be disposed of by approved waste receivers under the Waste Control Regulation (A.R. 192/1996).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Inspection certificate for the premises under the Alberta Fire Code (Safety Codes Act); structural load inspection and certification of racking, mezzanines, balers, and crane runways; workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (RSA 2000, c O-14.2) covering material handling, lockout/tagout, hot-work permits, and fall protection; Certificate of Recognition (COR) is recommended for yard operators and contractors.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; registration via Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and account administration through My Business Account (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers customs/export reporting through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) within the CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) platform. The Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) handles ULC incorporation records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Alberta ULC obtains its federal Business Number (BN) and the required program accounts (RC for corporate income tax, RT for GST/HST, RM for import/export) from the CRA. Procedure: (1) incorporate or continue the ULC under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) via the Alberta Corporate Registry and file the initial Alberta annual return; (2) register the federal BN online through the BRO portal or by filing Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number'; (3) activate the RT (GST/HST) program account, which is mandatory once CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Canada is exceeded; a non-resident-owned ULC must be prepared to post security (surety bond, irrevocable letter of credit, or cash) under ETA s. 241(1) where the Minister requires; (4) activate the RM import/export program account, enroll in CERS/CARM, and either obtain approved-exporter status or authorize a licensed customs broker/freight forwarder for electronic export declarations; (5) file the T2 corporate income tax return within six months after fiscal year-end and identify non-resident ownership schedules. Independently, the scrap-metal dealing activity requires a dealer licence under Alberta's Scrap Metals Dealers and Recyclers Act before commercial operations may commence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — For Canadian federal and Alberta income tax purposes, the Alberta ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation subject to entity-level Part I corporate income tax and Alberta corporate income tax (Alberta general rate 8%; small-business rate 2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; no Alberta capital tax or provincial sales tax). For US federal tax purposes, the Alberta ULC is not a per se corporation and is eligible, by election, for pass-through classification (disregarded entity or partnership), producing a cross-border hybrid entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (a) US Form 8832 check-the-box entity classification election, the controlling hybrid election, allowing a single-member ULC to be treated as a disregarded entity and a multi-member ULC as a partnership for US federal tax purposes; (b) Canada-US Tax Treaty Article IV(6) fiscally transparent entity treatment, permitting the US owner to claim treaty benefits on a look-through basis, subject to the hybrid mismatch rules in ITA ss. 94.3 and 18.6; (c) ETA s. 156 election for supplies of scrap or logistics services between the ULC and a closely related Canadian corporation to be treated as made for nil consideration; (d) ETA s. 150 election to align the GST/HST reporting period with the ULC's fiscal year.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating under the Bank of Canada Act, is the central monetary, exchange-rate, and foreign-reserve authority; exchange-rate policy and the Exchange Fund Account rest with the Minister of Finance, with the Bank of Canada acting as fiscal agent. Banking safety-and-soundness and licensed-institution supervision is delegated to the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering and cross-border transaction surveillance is administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); customs and export controls are administered by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) jointly with Global Affairs Canada. Canada has no separate central foreign-exchange control authority equivalent to a State Administration of Foreign Exchange.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is a fully convertible, free-floating currency; Canada observes IMF Article VIII and maintains no restrictions on payments and transfers for current international transactions and no capital controls. The Alberta ULC may freely remit dividends, royalties, management and franchise fees, interest on shareholder loans, and trade settlements to foreign parties without central-bank approval. Repatriation barriers are exclusively tax-driven under the Income Tax Act (Canada): non-resident withholding tax on dividends is normally 25%, treaty-reducible to 5% for a 10% corporate shareholder or 15% for portfolio holdings under the Canada-U.S. Income Tax Convention, with further optimization available if the ULC is treated as disregarded or flow-through for U.S. federal tax purposes. Intercompany pricing and thin capitalization must respect section 247 and the relevant Part XIII evidentiary requirements; cross-border wires of CAD 10,000 or more are informationally reportable to FINTRAC, but no exchange licence, quota, parity band, or conversion-ratio regime applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None statutory. Canada imposes no mandatory sale or surrender of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion into CAD, and no deadline for repatriation of foreign-currency receipts. The ULC may retain shredded-copper-scrap sale proceeds in USD or other foreign currency in a Canadian bank foreign-currency account, convert them at wholesale market rates at any time, or apply them directly to pay foreign suppliers, smelters, and freight costs. The controlling administrative requirements are informational: FINTRAC large-value transaction records for every wire of CAD 10,000 or more; CBSA cross-border currency and monetary-instrument declarations at the CAD 10,000 threshold; B13A export declarations through the Canadian Export Reporting System covering the consignment value and net mass; and the Statistics Canada export reporting questionnaire. No statutory conversion ratio exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for a secondary liquidity and FX-receivables channel; Low-Medium for the primary treasury spine. A fintech or electronic-money institution serving Canada must be registered with FINTRAC as a money service business and, if providing retail payment services, must comply with the Retail Payment Activities Act, and must clear through a licensed Canadian bank or an appropriately licensed foreign bank with a Canadian nexus. The Alberta ULC may lawfully open an EMI account (for example Wise, Airwallex, or similar digital platforms) for small receipts and for optimized FX spread at volumes below roughly CAD 500,000 per month. However, an EMI account is not a deposit account under the Bank Act, is not CDIC-insured, cannot serve as the issuing, confirming, or advising bank for a documentary letter of credit, and cannot lawfully hold a segregated capital-escrow balance with trust-like protection. EMI rails also tend to trigger enhanced due-diligence queries where the underlying settlement is physical scrap, and they generally do not provide a complete SWIFT gpi UETR trail or a direct correspondent-banking relationship with a trade-finance desk. The blueprint therefore mandates that the ULC maintain its primary operational, escrow, documentary-credit, and FX-hedging accounts at a Tier-1 Schedule I bank, with an EMI used only under a board-approved ancillary treasury policy and with funds moved through the same-day LVTS or ACH network to avoid breaching FINTRAC and bank concentration thresholds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is possible but conditional and must be delivered through an explicit enhanced-diligence path. For a non-resident-owned Alberta ULC, client-identification and verification obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act attach to the entity, each director, each authorized signatory, and every ultimate beneficial owner at 25% and 10% control or ownership thresholds. In current Tier-1 bank practice, overseas directors and UBOs may complete a bank-approved video KYC interview, but the practical mandate is that at least one officer with authority (usually a Canadian-resident director, the corporate secretary, or a registered agent) attends an in-branch session in Alberta for the initial account opening; alternatively, a notarized certified-copy identification pack (passport, proof of address) executed before a notary public in the home jurisdiction and delivered by bank-graded courier is accepted by most banks as the functional equivalent for remote opening. Mandatory corporate documentation includes an active Alberta Corporate Registry certificate of status or good standing, a registered office address in Alberta, a certificate of incumbency, a unanimous board resolution authorizing the account and its signatories, executed specimen signatures, the parent's audited financial statements or a banker's reference, and CRS or FATCA entity self-certification. Fully remote opening without any physical attendance is realistically achievable in 60-70% of similar ULC structures when a credible global banking relationship already exists and the account mandate is supported by an interbank opinion letter. The documentary-credit and receivable-financing facility will additionally require execution of the credit agreement, general security agreement, and an ISDA or IFEMA schedule, which may be e-signed under Alberta's Electronic Transactions Act if the bank accepts digital PKI signing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-based red flag: scrap and waste trading is classified Medium-Risk Enhanced because of high value-to-weight ratios, shredder and teardown ambiguity, mixed-material provenance, and the use of cash-heavy second-hand markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply-chain integrity dossier comprising (a) licensed scrap-dealer and recycler permits issued by the applicable Alberta or municipal authority; (b) weighbridge tickets and a mass-balance reconciliation reconciling every inbound scrap input to the outbound shredded copper wire output; (c) an approved-vendor register and inbound supplier contracts evidencing title; (d) independent laboratory certificates verifying copper content and absence of contaminants; (e) B13A customs export declarations for each consignment; (f) SGS, Intertek, or equivalent pre-shipment inspection reports; (g) the applicable Alberta Environment and Protected Areas permit for storage, processing, and pollution prevention; and (h) the ULC's written anti-money-laundering and metal-trading compliance manual, together with an independent third-party ESG or provenance opinion available on the bank's request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual cross-border wire pattern: high-frequency USD wire receipts from multiple offshore buyers in Asia and Eastern Europe into a newly opened ULC account, with settlement split between the Canadian bank and an FX fintech, triggering FINTRAC large-value monitoring and suspicion of trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-emptive treasury transparency pack containing: an expected monthly turnover and country-exposure letter approved by the ULC board; an approved-counterparty list with country-risk ratings; SWIFT gpi UETR records from prior completed scrap trades; a parent-bank reference evidencing 24 months of clean relationship conduct; a per-wire document set (commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, customs clearance, and weight certificate) matching each incoming payment; a treasury policy prohibiting payment splitting or unexplained third-party settlement; and a standing instruction to the bank's transaction-monitoring team that the compliance officer retains source-of-funds evidence for every wire equal to or above CAD 10,000. The pack is filed before the first peak-volume shipment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each anniversary date of incorporation or registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in compliance notices and administrative dissolution or strike-off after two consecutive annual returns remain outstanding; restoration requires prescribed filings and fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end; any corporate tax balance is generally due two months after year-end, or three months for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties generally apply where tax is owing, with arrears interest and possible gross-negligence penalties; persistent non-compliance may trigger enforcement and assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return, if the corporation has an annual filing period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally three months after the fiscal year-end for corporations, subject to the corporation's assigned GST/HST reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and arrears interest may apply; repeated non-compliance may result in reassessment, collection action, or cancellation of the GST/HST account.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Information Returns and Employee Statements, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of February following the calendar year in which remuneration was paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incorrect information-return penalties may apply, including penalties based on the number of slips and days overdue.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Alberta private corporation is generally not subject to a statutory independent audit solely because of revenue, assets, or employee thresholds. Auditor appointment may be required by the Alberta Business Corporations Act unless valid shareholder approval or an applicable exemption is available, and may also be required by shareholders, lenders, investors, securities rules, or contractual terms.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for eligible private entities; IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises and may be adopted where permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not generally require a separate annual public UBO filing for an Alberta corporation. The corporation must maintain accurate internal registers, ownership records, and beneficial-ownership information, document share transfers promptly, and update relevant tax, banking, and AML records when ownership or control changes. Federal corporations may be subject to separate Canada Business Corporations Act significant-control register requirements.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers and Securities Issuances
Minute Book containing directors' and shareholders' resolutions and meeting minutes
Articles, certificate of incorporation, bylaws, and amendments
Registered office and records office records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350-1,100 per year, depending on registered-office, records-office, nominee-director, mail-handling, and compliance-support services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-12,000 for a standard private-company audit; no audit fee if a valid exemption applies and no voluntary or contractual audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined standard combined rate (15% federal general corporate rate + 8% Alberta provincial flat rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction reduces federal rate to 9% on first CAD 500,000 active business income earned by a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC); Alberta small business rate reduces provincial rate to 2% on the same CAD 500,000 active business income bracket. No tax holidays for recycled copper scrap trading; income is taxable as ordinary business income. Manufacturer or wheeled-charge incentives unlikely for a trading entity. The Alberta Innovation Employment Grant (up to 20% of incremental R&D spend) is generally irrelevant to pure commodity trading. For a ULC, if held by a non-resident and considered a 'nitrate corporation' under the remittance regime, no branch tax concession is automatically granted; Alberta treats the ULC as a corporation resident in Canada if centrally managed and controlled in Canada. Input tax refunds under GST/HST are available to registrants on zero-rated qualifying export and transit supplies of scrap copper, impacting cashflow and taxable margin.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed electronically via GST/HST Internet File Transfer dedicated service, CRA My Business Account (MyBA) corporate portal, or approved third-party EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) software (e.g., Intuit QuickBooks, Aspire, Profile; mandatory electronic filing for gross revenue over CAD 1 million).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (12-month taxation year). Quarterly instalments required where net tax owing exceeds CAD 3,000 in the previous year or current year. Instalment payments due on the last day of each quarter of the taxation year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed within 6 months after the taxation year end. Example: a December 31 year-end files by June 30 of the following year. The balance of tax payable is due no later than 3 months after the tax year-end for all corporations other than CCPCs (CCPCs must pay within 3 months, but certain related corporations and small CCPCs may be eligible for the 6-month payment extension for amounts in excess of the prior-year instalment threshold).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, cost of goods sold, gross profit, total expenses, and net income before taxes per financial statements, prepared under IFRS or ASPE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must enter Canadian-source gross trading revenues only; revenues from off-shore resale of scrap copper purchased from unrelated third parties and shipped directly from non-Canadian origin may be excluded if no carrying-on-business in Canada. Use the 'business recognition' test under domestic law and tie-breaker under the Canada–US Treaty if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments from net income to taxable income, including permanent differences, non-deductible expenses, and Part IV dividend refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the ULC, add back unusual non-tax-deductible reserves; subtract any Canadian dividend refund for intercorporate dividends. No treaty-based adjustment should be made here. For a ULC claiming to be residence in Canada (management and control in Alberta), use ordinary Schedule 1 reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal basic tax computed at 38% of taxable income, reduced by federal abatement (10% of taxable income allocable to a province), general reduction, and small business deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident corporate shareholder is seeking an exemption under the Canada–US Treaty, the ULC's income reported at Box 700 is nevertheless taxable under Part I if the ULC is resident in Canada. Non-resident allocates income under treaty business profits provisions only if a permanent establishment exists in Canada; otherwise the ULC itself remains taxable on global income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 1, Item 1 (Net federal tax payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net federal tax payable after deductions: abatement (Schedule 4), general reduction (Schedule 27), small business deduction (Schedule 27), and investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned ULC should not claim the federal abatement for income earned through an Alberta PE unless Alberta tax was allocable. File Schedule 4 to allocate taxable income to Alberta using gross revenue and salaries/wages in Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 400 (Alberta corporate tax and tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta taxable income and provincial tax computed at 8%, plus the Alberta small business deduction for eligible CCPC active business income (first CAD 500,000, effective provincial rate 2%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled ULCs are not CCPCs and are not eligible for the Alberta small business deduction; schedule the full 8% rate. Alberta filed returns are integrated into the T2 filing through CRA, no separate provincial return is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T106 (Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of cross-border transactions with non-arm's length non-residents and notional movements of amounts (e.g., management fees, intercompany financing, or scrap purchases/sales).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for transactions where the total amount paid/receivable/receivable in respect of a taxpayer, a non-resistant beneficiary, and the non-resident's related enterprise exceeds CAD 50,000 in the taxation year in any single class of transactions (including loans and advances). The ULC must identify the nature of the transaction, the arm's-length methodology used, and the Canadian legal entity files.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 88 (Transfer Pricing Disclosure) and Form RC4645 (Transfer Pricing Penalty Waiver Request)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of transfer-pricing adjustments and penalties, and application for waiver where adjustment below CAD 50,000 penalty threshold and documentation satisfies conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the ULC applies the transactional net margin method (TNMM) for scrap purchases from a related offshore affiliate, include segmented financials and comparability adjustments. Verify that a separate T106 is filed for each transaction line; late-filing penalties apply to each non-filed T106 (CAD 25 per day up to 2,500, plus 500 for the first incorrect return, 1,000 for subsequent).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing: 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months. Where the T2 was previously penalized in any prior 3-year period, the penalty is doubled (10% plus 2% per month up to 24 months). Daily penalty of CAD 25 for non-filing of a T106 (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500), plus CAD 500 or CAD 1,000 for knowingly false information. Interest accrues at the prescribed rate on unpaid tax and penalties: base prescribed rate + 4% for corporate tax; current quarterly prescribed rates are posted by CRA (approx. 7%–9% effective 2025). Late payment of instalments triggers interest beginning on the instalment due date, regardless of the later final return deadline. The Canada Revenue Agency additionally charges a late-filing penalty for failure to file T2 where the corporation has previously filed with the 'special elections' subsection; no multiple municipalities apply. Tax evasion for a materially false return (e.g., omitted scrap trading income) is a separate criminal offence under s. 239 ITA, punishable by a fine of 50%–200% of the tax sought to be evaded and up to 5 years imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on taxable Canadian dividends paid to a non-resident shareholder (including any deemed dividend arising on a ULC redemption/repurchase of shares). The rate is applicable on the gross dividend amount unless a treaty reduces it.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Canada–United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended by the 2023 Protocol) limits the dividend withholding tax to 5% where the non-resident corporation is a beneficial owner that owns directly at least 10% of the voting shares of the Canadian paying corporation and meets the 365-day holding period; otherwise 15% for portfolio dividends. For Canadian resident (including Alberta ULC) distributions to a U.S. parent resident in the U.S., the reduced 5% rate is available automatically via a CRA T2 return claiming the treaty; must provide the U.S. taxpayer's IRS Form 8832 or Form 1120 evidence, plus a completed Form 1136? In practice, submit on paper the T2 treaty exemption (Schedule 90, Treaty-Based Non-Resident Corporation Election) and the non-resident shareholder must provide an annual Form NR301, NR302, or Department of Finance certificate of residency letter (TRC). The TRC must be electronically obtained from the IRS with a valid 6166 letter. The paying Alberta ULC must withhold at the statutory 25% unless the treaty relief process is satisfied prior to payment; CRA may accept an expedited application through the Letter of Substantiation procedure (Form T1001). Upon receiving the TRC, the non-resident files a Form F105N or applies under the Treaty-Withholding Tax Refund Procedure within 3 years to claim the excess. For countries with a comprehensive DTA with Canada, the same 5%/15% rates apply on dividends under Article 10, requiring the non-resident to obtain an official TRC from its tax authority and attach it to the CRA form NR301 (Authorized Representative) or Form T-TRC.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: Part XIII 25% on royalties and interest paid by a Canadian resident to a non-resident (subject to exceptions for arm's-length interest paid to a non-resident arm's-length lender not subject to Canadian business, and for 'treaty-exempt' interest under U.S./Canada treaty). Canada–US Treaty: 0% on interest and royalties paid to a U.S. resident (4-year old zero for royalties; 0% for interest, effective for amounts arising after 2008; royalty rate for industrial royalties 10% until the 2019 Protocol zeroed all royalties). In practice, for Canada to a U.S. parent, interest and royalties are 0% if the recipient is a U.S. resident and beneficial owner. For a non-treaty jurisdiction, 25% applies. Interest with respect to accounts payable for purchases of scrap copper is subject to the participation exemption only if the interest is deductible under Part I and satisfies the arm's-length thin cap and withholding 25% unless treaty-reduced.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory minimum transaction threshold requiring contemporaneous TP documentation under Canadian law (ITA s.247(3)). The Canada Revenue Agency expects all taxpayers engaged in cross-border non-arm's length transactions to prepare complete and accurate documentation, sufficient to earn a penalty waiver, reflecting 10 comparable years; a T106 return is mandatory for any particular transaction exceeding CAD 50,000. Canada's TCP 'Local File'/'Master File' framework applies to taxpayers with annual gross revenue exceeding CAD 50 million or cross-border related-party transactions exceeding CAD 1 million, equivalent to CAD 1,000,000 (as per CRA administrative practice mirroring G20 final report; no explicit SEP). For smaller companies, CRA uses a materiality threshold of CAD 50,000 per transaction and public companies must file a Schedule 88.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Canada does not have a general Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code similar to the UAE, the principles of economic substance are embedded in Canadian income tax law through the concept of 'carrying on business', the 'sham doctrine', 'ineffective transactions' under GAAR (s.245 ITA), and the non-resident trust attribution rules (s.94). An Alberta ULC used solely to invoice scrap copper purchases/sales with no commercial activity will be reassessed under the 'agency/permanent establishment' provisions and is exposed to the misapplication of the treaty's 'business profits' article. CRA will apply a substance-over-form test requiring actual management, personnel, and asset in Canada. For the ULC to claim treaty benefits, it must pass a 'purpose' test under the Canada–US treaty's limitation-on-benefits provisions in Article 29: the Preamble and Ownership/Base Erosion tests require the ULC to have a genuine business in Alberta; a shell ULC with no trading, storage, or contractual enforcement functions is a red flag. ERP on 'commercial circular metals trading' requires the ULC to maintain physical stock records, scale weight certificates, supplier contracts, and negotiate terms from Alberta.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Categorically understating revenue derived from Canadian-source scrap copper consignment sales or inflating cost of goods sold by recording false invoices from offshore agents for non-existent scrap purchases; deliberately omitting Part XIII withholding on dividends paid to a non-resident parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA s.239(1), a fine of CAD 4,000 to 20,000 plus 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to 5 years. Under s.163(2), civil penalty of the greater of CAD 100 and 10% of the understatement (50% if the misstatement was made knowingly; the penalty increases to 50% of tax sought to be evaded where fraud). Full reassessment limitations extended to any time in case of fraud or misrepresentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of substantial gross negligence with CRA issuance of an assessment can be jointly liable under the wire of having participated in the negligence; the CRA will apply 'knowingly, or under circumstances of gross negligence' standard. Criminal prosecution can pierce the corporate veil and cause the director to be personally restored for fines, unremitted source withholding, and Part XIII tax; travel bans under the Extradition act for foreign directors absent from Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Penalty and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation for cross-border purchases of recycled copper wire from a related non-resident supplier, using key non-arm's length prices (e.g., intentionally above CAD 5.00/kg to shift taxable income offshore).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA s.247(3), the Canadian taxpayer is subject to a transfer-pricing penalty of 10% of the amount of net transfer pricing adjustment in excess of the lesser of CAD 50,000 and 10% of the gross adjustments. Where documentation is missing, the penalty may be imposed without the net adjustment threshold. Adjustments also trigger resourcing and potential double taxation unless a corresponding adjustment is obtained under the treaty MAP process.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for transfer pricing penalties, but if the company is insolvent, CRA can claim for the corporate tax debt under the statutory 'directors' liability' rules (s.227.1 ITA) for unremitted Part XIII withholding tax and GST/HST. Directors who deliberately signed false T106 declarations are subject to indictable fraud under s.380 Criminal Code and s.495 ITA for complicity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The ULC serves as an artificial contractually staged intermediary between an offshore scrap broker and the end-buyer, with no physical or economic activities in Alberta (no office, no staff, no risk management, no trade insurance, no purchase of copper inventory). CRA recharacterizes the transactions under the sham doctrine and GAAR (s.245) as numbers-only invoicing from a bare benefit company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under s.245 reassessment ignoring the sale agency and eliminating the ULC's gross profit; penalties and interest restored. The company's deduction of expenses is denied; the transaction is reconstructed as if the ULC never existed; non-resident is taxed under force-of-attraction rules. A GAAR penalty of 25% of the transaction benefit (under s.245(5)) applies to the planning. If misrepresentation is found, the Criminal Code prohibits any false document with intent to defraud under s.380 — count as an indictable offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Judicial piercing of the corporate veil where the ULC is an agent or simplicitic instrument will make the non-resident parent directly responsible for Canadian tax under the 'thin capitalization' and 'agency' rules. Directors are personally liable for withholding taxes and for any GST/HST remitted amounts; travel restrictions and asset freezes can follow from a recovery action. For abusive domestic disguised AG, CRA may also issue an immediate 'Canada Revenue Act' assessment and apply a 25% gross-negligence penalty 25% of tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering for Physical Commodity Trading
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a recycled scrap copper trading business with cash flow that is structurally inconsistent with the volume of shipments or purchases, using offshore shell accounts, incomplete CMRs and invoice packing lists, or accepting settlement to unrelated third-party bank accounts. Failing to register as a money services business (MSB) and to conduct CDD for counterparties in the medium-risk enhanced AML tier as confirmed in the pipeline metadata.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), failure to report suspicious transactions is a summary offence punishable by fine CAD 250,000 and up to 5 years imprisonment for individuals; for corporations, penalties of up to CAD 500,000 per violation. CRA-completed shell company with no commercial substance triggers Qualified Income Tax fraud and the Minister of Public Safety can issue a Certificate of Permanent Realization prohibiting export of gold or copper. Enforcement agencies may require retroactive risk assessment, penalties from Fintrac, and referral to the RCMP International Financial Crimes Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally charged with money laundering under s.462.31 of the Criminal Code if they directed a transaction involving property derived from a designated offence; maximum imprisonment of 10 years. Directors who fail to apply AML safeguards (due diligence, travel risk, and compliance) are exposed to Fintrac's individual penalties of up to CAD 500,000. A travel ban may be issued pending criminal investigation; corporate dissolution is not a shield while assets are in the hands of the de facto controller.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding / Part XIII and T106 Non-Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold 25% on dividends declared to the non-resident parent, or advising the internal group that a ULC is 'transparent' thereby avoiding withholding on deemed distributions; also failing to file T106 for cross-border loans exceeding CAD 50,000 or for intercompany supply of copper wire with a related party.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: An assessment under Part XIII imposes the full 25% withholding tax on the gross amount paid or credited; plus interest at the prescribed rate. A penalty for failure to withhold is 10% of the tax withheld (or 20% day). For T106 late filing, a flat CAD 25 daily penalty up to CAD 2,500, plus CAD 500 for a first inaccurate filing and CAD 1,000 for each subsequent incorrect T106. For a dedicated ECI group, non-compliance can amount to a 'willful non-filing' under s.238, a strict liability offence leading to fine and potential imprisonment for officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally liable for the corporation's failure to remit source deductions and Part XIII withholding tax under s.227.1 ITA without any burden to prove due diligence. The corporate veil does not prevent CRA from issuing a Notice of Personal Liability, and the 'due diligence' defence is limited. If the dividend was paid while the corporation was insolvent, a fraudulent conveyance claim may be made against the recipient.
